name: Skin fragility-woolly hair-palmoplantar keratoderma syndrome
aliases: Skin fragility with woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma
Woolly hair-palmoplantar keratoderma syndrome with skin fragility

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for Skin fragility-woolly hair-palmoplantar keratoderma syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of tightly curled, woolly hair from birth or early infancy
Diffuse or focal palmoplantar keratoderma with hyperkeratosis
Marked skin fragility with blistering and erosions upon minor trauma
Nail abnormalities including dystrophy or thickening
Skin biopsy showing epidermolysis or keratinocyte abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: woolly hair, palmoplantar keratoderma, and skin fragility
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Tightly curled, fragile hair evident from birth
Thickened skin on palms and soles with hyperkeratosis
searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles
widespread hand and foot skin thickening

pathognomonic.notes: Blisters and erosions develop after minor trauma

common.notes: Excessive sweating of palms and soles
Hyperkeratotic plaques around mouth and eyes
searchTerms: thickened skin around mouth and eyes
scaly skin plaques on face edges

occasional.notes: Inflammation and erosions of the lips
Reduced sweating outside palms and soles
searchTerms: reduced sweating outside hands and feet
less sweating on body areas except palms and soles
dry skin due to low sweat
blisters on palms and soles with infection
infected blisters on hands and feet

rare.notes: Erosions affecting oral or genital mucosa

laboratory: Histopathology showing epidermal cleavage or keratinocyte fragility
other: Hair shaft microscopy showing woolly hair abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: More generalized skin blistering without woolly hair
Woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy

redFlags: Severe skin blistering leading to secondary infection
Rapid progression of palmoplantar keratoderma with pain
Signs of cardiac involvement (arrhythmia or syncope) suggesting overlap with cardiocutaneous syndromes
references: Orphanet: Skin fragility-woolly hair-palmoplantar keratoderma syndrome, ORPHA:293165
Uitto J, et al. Molecular genetics of skin fragility disorders. J Invest Dermatol. 2020.
McGrath JA, et al. Woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma syndromes: clinical and molecular insights. Clin Dermatol. 2019.
